answer: To resist Sybil attacks, the network applies topological cut verifications across interaction graphs, partitioning synthetic clusters along sparse cuts. Independent peer committees perform game-theoretic multi-agent auditing, subjecting suspicious clusters to stake slashing. Like dense shale resisting erosion, the protocol binds agents with ferrous proof commitments under sable cryptographic signatures. Because cross-verification requires unique bonded edges across sparse cuts, orchestrating fake identities imposes a superlinear attacker cost scaling with $O(N^2)$ staked bonds.
